title: Managed Material Delta
purpose: Defines the normative classification of initializer-managed differences between accepted baseline and reconciliation-target framework inventories.

normative_requirements.text: A managed-material delta shall be derived from two authoritative repo-spec initialization inventory endpoints: the material/output inventories associated with the target repository's active accepted baseline framework revision and the corresponding inventories associated with the supplying reconciliation-target framework revision.

Stable `material_key` identity shall be the primary correspondence key between baseline and reconciliation-target inventories; raw Git path differences alone shall not establish managed-material identity or upgrade authority.

Each material identity in the union of the two inventory endpoints shall receive exactly one deterministic directional classification applicable to the accepted inventory model: unchanged, added, modified, removed, or retargeted.

An added classification means a managed material identity is absent from the baseline inventory and present in the reconciliation-target inventory; removed means present in baseline and absent from target; unchanged means the accepted material definition is equivalent across both endpoints.

A modified classification means the same stable managed-material identity remains applicable but one or more authoritative material attributes or source content identities require reconciliation; a retargeted classification means stable identity is retained while its governed destination mapping changes.

The delta shall not include arbitrary target-repository paths that are not represented within initializer-managed inventory authority, even when those paths differ from the supplying repo-spec checkout.

Delta classification alone shall not authorize mutation; source-owned upgrade qualification, target-local managed-state checks, staging, and later validation gates may further restrict the legal reconciliation set.

conformance.rationale: Current accepted repo-spec authority declares no governed generic product implementation-test obligation for this requirement at product/scripts/test-product; source-development tests and validation self-tests are separate surfaces. Future activation requires a governed correspondence update.
